scope: Actual Cedar2.0 libVE ABI review, private WC allocator build/mock validation, current kernel integration review, and 30-frame NV21 acceptance preparation. No board operation by this reviewer.

actual_libve.method: SDK AArch64 objdump disassembly plus same-package headers and Tina sun60iw2 driver/DTS comparison
actual_libve.get_env: ioctl 0x101; 24-byte structure; mmap address from +8; zero-filled kernel response matches donor
actual_libve.decoder_top_offset: ioctl 0x804 return value; decoder default 0, encoder ve2 has 0x800 and is a separate device
actual_libve.phy_offset_rule: VeInitialize stores ctx+172: version==0x1639 => 0x20000000; version>0x1718 => 0; other low versions => 0x40000000. Not controlled by CdcIonGetMemType.
actual_libve.runtime_guard: WC MemAdapter logs actual version/phy_offset and rejects any nonzero offset.
actual_libve.headers: sc_interface.h, veInterface.h, vencoder.h, vdecoder.h and memoryAdapter.h compared byte-for-byte with matching SDK source headers
actual_libve.source_limit: GetVeOpsS implementation was not found in available Tina multimedia source; original libVE is retained unchanged.

candidate_mock_validation.scope: Actual final ARM64 candidate libraries under QEMU; VE/heap mocked; no hardware visibility acceptance

compile_warning_limit: Base retained vendor CdcIonIsLegacy pointer-cast and iniparser sprintf warnings; MemAdapter compiled without warnings. No claim of complete vendor-source Werror cleanliness.

checks: Same TGID supports multiple VE opens and decoder/allocator worker threads; original libVE also shares its process-global fd.
24-byte GET_ENV, 4KiB MMIO mapping at offset 0, decoder top offset 0, H264/top lock bits, and 0x502/503 match actual libVE.
Heap allocations use the same VE device with dma_alloc_wc/dma_mmap_wc; only same-device private dma-buf imports are accepted. No system-heap or foreign-buffer bypass.
32-bit complete allocation range and contiguous identity scatterlist addresses are checked.
Every successfully imported or potentially disclosed DMA allocation retains backing until reboot, including normal release and partial copy_to_user failure; total budget 128MiB.
Userland flush checks complete range belongs to its active allocation and issues dmb osh ordering. Kernel heap CPU begin/end and cache ioctl provide barriers. This is not CPU cache invalidation.
Userland fd/mmap cleanup does not recycle kernel-pinned backing; failure/timeout poison prevents new decoder sessions.
limits: No proven AXI drain; reset assertion or elapsed delay is not a reuse guarantee.
No actual VE version, DMA visibility, IRQ completion or frame correctness has been measured by this reviewer.
Root and other reviewers own provider/reset/PPU details and whole-kernel validation.

single_decode.frame_number_review: Vendor increments nDispFrameCount before save interval check; -ss 0 would save only 29 frames. Start 1 saves 1..30; finish cap 31 permits EOS drain of the 30-frame B-frame fixture.
pass_conditions: Exact approved bundle manifest and all 34 file hashes
Exact compressed and reference fixture hashes
Exactly 3456000 NV21 output bytes and all 30 frames byte-identical
Actual WC version/zero offset marker and validated WC ordering barrier marker

gate_test.scope: Host-only mocked acceptance-gate tests: valid evidence, corrupted output, no IRQ, nonzero offset, missing barrier, failed child, timeout/exit race, and surviving child. Not a hardware decode.

encoding.needs: Separate ve2 encoder registers, IRQ48, VE_ENC power and validation; decoder success is insufficient.

playback_and_browser: Next useful route after direct decode is explicit GStreamer omxh264dec afbc=false linear output, then GstGL display. Current OpenMAX bridge does not automatically accelerate FFmpeg/Firefox; no browser backend or VAAPI implementation is claimed.
privacy: Tina remains read-only. Full vendor source copies and proprietary binary bundles remain private build artifacts, outside public source backup.
